basis: Rahab's red cord read as redemptive blood
note: The commentary's cord marks a household's rescue from destruction; 1 Clement reads the scarlet cord as a sign of redemption through the Lord's blood, changing a rescue marker into a Christian theological sign.

basis: strong sustain weak and rich provide for poor
note: The commentary makes the steep path communal with burdens and feeding; Clement urges strong people to care for weak people and wealthy people to provide for poor people.

basis: share possessions with a brother
note: The commentary's exchange of sustaining things makes individuals a community; the Didache tells a believer to share possessions with a brother and avoid calling them exclusively one's own.

basis: Members care for one another
note: The commentary’s mutual counsel makes the group interdependent; Paul says the body’s members should have the same care for one another.

basis: members suffer and rejoice together
note: The commentary moves from a solitary person into joined lives; Paul says all members suffer when one suffers and rejoice when one is honoured.

basis: love itself acts patiently
note: The commentary treats patience as a communal virtue maintained between people; Paul calls love patient, placing endurance in a relationship rather than isolated self-control.

basis: Love rejoices with truth
note: The commentary makes truth the content of mutual counsel; Paul says love rejoices with the truth, placing truthful conduct inside communal ethics.

basis: Love bears and endures all things
note: The commentary presents patience as a quality exchanged within the community; Paul describes love as bearing and enduring all things, a sustained communal form of sabr.

basis: Steadfast work is not in vain
note: The commentary says most human effort is loss but closes with faithful work and patience; Paul calls believers steadfast and abundant in the Lord’s work, assuring them that such labor is not empty.

basis: The Day tests each person’s work
note: The commentary imagines deeds fitting like building material and truth as the day of reckoning; Paul says the Day reveals each builder’s work and fire tests it.

basis: the day and fire test each person's work
note: The commentary's later judgment exposes the value of fitted work; Paul says the day discloses each builder's work as fire tests its quality.

basis: work burns and builder suffers loss
note: The commentary sees a lifetime's work destroyed just when its value is tested; Paul says a builder whose work burns suffers loss though he himself is saved.

basis: coming day discloses hidden motives
note: The commentary's haqq is the day when each person confronts what was done; Paul says the Lord will bring hidden things to light and disclose the intentions of hearts.

basis: bought with a price, do not become slaves
note: The commentary's ascent connects market exchange to freedom from bondage; Paul uses purchase language to forbid renewed human enslavement.

basis: The world’s form is passing away
note: The commentary treats time and worldly capital as expiring; Paul tells believers to use the world without clinging to it because its present form is passing.

basis: love in deed and truth rather than words only
note: The commentary refuses to separate mutual counsel of truth from rightly fitted acts; this verse expressly joins truth, action and love among siblings.

basis: People built together as living stones
note: The commentary pictures righteous action as bricks set in place; Peter calls believers living stones being built into a spiritual house, making the community itself constructed.

basis: living stones built into one house
note: The commentary likens fitting good works and joined believers to building blocks; Peter describes believers as living stones being built into a spiritual house.

basis: divine patience waits while ark is built
note: The commentary's patience holds life secure while a weak refuge fails; Peter recalls divine patience during ark construction before the flood, linking endurance to a built shelter.

basis: gifts received and passed as entrusted service
note: The commentary's truth and patience move between people like a kept trust; Peter calls each person to serve others with a received gift as a steward.

basis: encourage and build each other up
note: The commentary says people fit together like building material and pass counsel between them; Paul tells them to encourage one another and build each other up.

basis: Encourage the weak and be patient with all
note: The commentary’s community counsels patience; Paul joins encouraging the fainthearted and helping the weak to the instruction to be patient with everyone.

basis: admonish, help weak and be patient with all
note: The commentary pairs reciprocal advice with patience and care for vulnerable people; Paul joins these commands in one instruction to the community.

basis: people of day rather than night
note: The commentary likens members of the final community to night and day arranged together; Paul calls his audience children of light and of day, giving the adjacent exhortation in 1 Thessalonians 5:11 a temporal setting.

basis: uncertain riches versus secure trust
note: The commentary's capital can be lost despite having been stored; Paul tells the wealthy to set hope on God rather than the uncertainty of riches.

basis: rich instructed to do good and share readily
note: The commentary moves from endangered capital into communal good works; Paul orders the rich to be generous and ready to share.

basis: Good works stored as future treasure
note: The commentary makes righteous deeds the secure yield of mortal time; Timothy tells the rich to be rich in good works and store treasure for the future.

basis: sharing stores a firm foundation for future life
note: The commentary turns spent capital into an enduring good through deeds; Paul says generous people store a foundation for the future and take hold of life.

basis: guard the entrusted deposit
note: The commentary ends with an essence carefully held and conveyed; Timothy is again addressed as custodian of what has been entrusted to him, a separate recurrence from 2 Timothy 1:14.

basis: seal and guarantee placed in hearts
note: The commentary gives sabr the secondary sense of guarantor and sealed contents; Paul depicts God sealing believers and giving the Spirit as a guarantee in their hearts.

basis: outward wasting and daily inner renewal
note: The commentary's human principal erodes during time while a substance is preserved; Paul describes the outer person wasting away as the inner person is renewed day by day.

basis: Light affliction and a weight of glory
note: The commentary joins time’s pressure to scales and loss; Paul contrasts brief affliction with an eternal weight of glory, reversing the apparent measure of value.

basis: pressure produces eternal weight
note: The commentary moves from pressure and light scales to enduring value; Paul says temporary affliction produces an incomparable eternal weight of glory.

basis: Pressed but not crushed
note: The commentary opens with pressure that can destroy accumulated yield; Paul describes believers as hard pressed but not crushed, distinguishing pressure from final loss.

basis: painful sorrow leads to repentance and rescue
note: The commentary's bitter retained counsel serves endurance rather than waste; Paul distinguishes godly sorrow that produces repentance and salvation from sorrow that produces death.

basis: painful letter causes useful grief
note: The commentary's preserved bitter medicine is corrective speech; Paul admits his letter grieved its recipients, then treats the short grief as part of their recovery.

basis: one group's surplus supplies another's lack
note: The commentary turns loss into shared provision through reciprocal action; Paul describes present abundance covering another group's need and future reciprocity.

basis: Self-control and endurance after faith
note: The commentary’s believers join faith to good action and sabr; Peter’s sequence adds self-control and endurance to faith-informed virtue.

basis: entrusted deposit kept until that day
note: The commentary connects keeping an entrusted essence with the day that reveals deeds; Paul says the one he trusts can guard his deposit until that day.

basis: guard the entrusted good deposit
note: The commentary ends with an essence kept and passed rather than spent; Timothy is ordered to guard a received deposit through the Holy Spirit.

basis: Entrusted teaching passed to further teachers
note: The commentary ends with truth and patience changing hands; Paul tells Timothy to entrust what he heard to faithful people able to teach others, an explicit chain of transmission.

basis: entrust teaching to people who will teach others
note: The commentary's truth and patience are handed onward and kept; Timothy must entrust received teaching to reliable people able to teach still others.

basis: completed race and retained faith
note: The commentary turns spent time into a sustained course ending with what remains; Paul says he has finished the race and kept the faith.

basis: day of just judge and kept reward
note: The commentary's decisive day confronts a person's completed work; Paul expects a crown on that day from the righteous judge after retaining faith in 2 Timothy 4:7.

basis: support others and become fellow workers for truth
note: The commentary has truth passed hand to hand in a working community; the letter says supporting travelling workers makes the supporters coworkers with truth.

basis: resources distributed by need
note: The commentary's community exchanges what preserves others after loss; the Jerusalem group lays sale proceeds before the apostles for distribution according to need.

basis: record of debt cancelled
note: The commentary joins debt, entrustment and release; Paul depicts a hostile written record of obligations as cancelled and removed, extending the debt image to deliverance.

basis: love binds the group into completeness
note: The commentary's rope scene turns separate people into a fitted company; Paul calls love the bond of perfection over the community's other virtues.

basis: teach and admonish one another
note: The commentary's final verse passes haqq through reciprocal counsel; Paul asks the word to dwell in the group as members teach and admonish each other.

basis: Truth heard, believed, and sealed
note: The commentary gathers belief, truth, and what is kept; Ephesians says its readers heard the word of truth, believed, and were sealed with the promised Spirit.

basis: truth heard, belief followed by sealing
note: The commentary joins faith, transmitted truth and the image of a sealed store; Paul says believers heard the word of truth, believed and were sealed with the promised Spirit.

basis: A seal that guarantees inheritance
note: The commentary calls patience a guarantor and ends with what is preserved; Ephesians calls the Spirit the guarantee of inheritance until redemption.

basis: building fitted together and growing
note: The commentary compares righteous works and persons to bricks settling in place; Paul says the whole structure is joined together and grows into a holy temple.

basis: people built together into a dwelling
note: The commentary says individuals fit into one community like placed bricks; Paul says his addressees are built together into a dwelling for God.

basis: Each part builds the whole body
note: The commentary’s believers add to one another; Paul’s body is joined through each supporting part and builds itself up in love.

basis: joined body builds itself through each part's work
note: The commentary's separate people become a working whole; Paul says each part contributes to the joined body's growth in love.

basis: Patience expressed by bearing with one another
note: The commentary turns patience into reciprocal communal counsel; Paul joins humility, patience, and bearing with one another in love.

basis: Truth spoken among interdependent members
note: The commentary turns truth into reciprocal counsel within a community; Paul says to speak truth with one’s neighbor because members belong to one another.

basis: speak truth to neighbour because members belong together
note: The commentary shifts from the lone human to a mutually bound group handing on truth; Paul grounds truthful speech in shared membership.

basis: Unity held by a bond of peace
note: The commentary pictures people holding together; Paul urges preservation of the Spirit’s unity through a bond of peace.

basis: unity kept by bond of peace
note: The commentary's common grasp replaces enmity with brotherhood; Paul urges the community to maintain the Spirit's unity in the bond of peace.

basis: Time treated as something to redeem
note: The commentary calls time capital that can be spent or lost; Paul urges believers to make the most of the time because the days are evil, giving time an explicit economic value.

basis: Freedom from slavery’s yoke
note: The commentary makes freeing a captive the answer to the steep ascent; Paul says Christ set people free and warns them not to return to a yoke of slavery.

basis: freedom expressed by serving one another
note: The commentary's released captive enters a community of mutual responsibility; Paul tells freed people to use freedom to serve one another in love.

basis: patience is fruit borne by a community
note: The commentary ends with patience kept as an enduring yield; Paul includes patience among the Spirit's fruit alongside love and peace.

basis: community restores someone caught in a fault
note: The commentary's group saves a person from a figurative edge through shared counsel; Paul tells spiritually mature members to restore the person caught in transgression gently.

basis: Bear one another’s burdens
note: The commentary turns from the isolated person to mutual counsel; Paul tells the community to carry one another’s burdens, making shared endurance an enacted duty.

basis: bear one another's burdens
note: The commentary's steep path becomes a shared journey with a load; Paul commands the community to carry one another's burdens.

basis: Patient good work bears a later harvest
note: The commentary closes with deeds and patience transmitted together; Paul urges persistence in doing good because a harvest comes in its season if people do not give up.

basis: Provoke one another to good works
note: The commentary makes mutual counsel issue in righteous action; Hebrews says to consider how to spur one another toward love and good works.

basis: consider how to stir love and good works
note: The commentary passes counsel into fitting deeds within a group; Hebrews asks people to consider one another so love and good works result.

basis: assemble and encourage as the day approaches
note: The commentary's people preserve each other through diminishing time toward a decisive day; Hebrews connects gathering, mutual encouragement and the approaching day.

basis: Endurance after doing God’s will
note: The commentary closes with good action and patience held together; Hebrews says endurance is needed after doing God’s will in order to receive what is promised.

basis: Rahab's survival attributed to faith and welcome
note: The commentary's rope and shared refuge secure a household; Hebrews reads Rahab's non-destruction through her faith and reception of the spies, adding a faith reading to the cord scene.

basis: Lay aside weight and run with endurance
note: The commentary makes the steep ascent a road with a load; Hebrews tells runners to lay aside every weight and run the set race with endurance.

basis: painful discipline later yields righteous fruit
note: The commentary treats patience as a bitter essence preserved for benefit; Hebrews says discipline hurts now yet later yields peaceful fruit of righteousness.

basis: Esau trades birthright for one meal
note: The commentary's bad bargain spends enduring capital on brief satisfaction; Hebrews uses Esau's single meal as the warning's concrete transaction.

basis: remember prisoners as fellow prisoners
note: The commentary turns the captive's release into shared responsibility; Hebrews asks readers to remember prisoners as though imprisoned with them.

basis: Daily mutual exhortation prevents hardening
note: The commentary’s community advises one another; Hebrews commands daily encouragement so that no one is hardened by sin’s deceit, specifying both the repeated action and its danger.

basis: exhort one another every day
note: The commentary reads the last verse as reciprocal transfer across passing time; Hebrews commands daily mutual exhortation so no one hardens through sin.

basis: Faith and patience inherit promises
note: The commentary’s final community joins belief and patience; Hebrews says faith and patience characterize those who inherit the promises.

basis: Jesus as guarantor of a better covenant
note: The commentary’s secondary guarantor image meets Hebrews’ explicit description of Jesus as guarantor, applying financial surety language to the covenant.

basis: Death activates a will or covenant
note: The commentary’s death-triggered bequest meets Hebrews’ use of Greek diathēkē as a will: the writer uses the testator’s death to explain how the covenant takes effect.

basis: death required in a testament argument
note: The commentary combines death and entrusted last instructions; Hebrews treats a testament as requiring the death of its maker in its covenant argument.

basis: A will takes effect after death
note: The commentary’s bequest is activated by impending death; Hebrews’ next legal step says a will takes effect only after death, sharpening the contrast between present custody and later transfer.

basis: testament operative after death
note: The commentary's bequest becomes urgent at death; Hebrews says a testament takes effect upon death, sharpening the relation between dying and transfer.

basis: testing faith produces endurance
note: The commentary treats sabr as the retained product of pressure on faith; James states that the testing of faith produces steadfastness.

basis: endurance completes its work
note: The commentary joins patience to rightly fitted works; James lets endurance have its full work so a person becomes complete and lacking nothing.

basis: words of blessing without food fail hungry people
note: The commentary's mutual exhortation follows the actual feeding of the hungry; James exposes a verbal blessing that supplies neither clothing nor daily food.

basis: Rahab's rescue linked to sheltering messengers
note: The commentary's cord-marked house joins safety to deeds; James interprets Rahab's reception and dispatch of the messengers as active righteousness.

basis: A year of trade and expected profit
note: The commentary treats time as capital; James depicts merchants planning a year in a city to trade and make profit, exposing life’s plans to uncertainty.

basis: Life as a passing mist
note: The commentary reads the time of a human life as brief and vulnerable; James calls life a vapor that appears briefly and then vanishes.

basis: planned profitable future cut short by brief life
note: The commentary locates human loss inside spent time; James challenges merchants planning another trading year by saying they cannot know tomorrow and life is a vapour.

basis: bring wanderer back from ruin
note: The commentary's reciprocal advice prevents a fall into loss; James says turning a sinner from a wandering path saves a soul from death.

basis: withheld harvest wages cry out in judgment
note: The commentary's orchard yield meets bad market accounting and the final day; James says field workers' withheld pay cries out against wealthy landowners.

basis: Crop, rain, and patience
note: The commentary joins rain, fruit, and sabr; James tells the farmer to wait patiently for the precious crop until it receives the early and late rains, making delay before yield the point.

basis: patient farmer waits for precious crop and rains
note: The commentary ties patience to rain, fruit, useful yield and passing time; James makes a farmer waiting for rains and harvest the model for patient endurance.

basis: joined vine branches bear fruit
note: The commentary joins fruitful work to secure belonging; Jesus describes branches bearing much fruit only while abiding in the vine, making connection the source of yield.

basis: unfruitful branch cast away and burned
note: The commentary's loss links failing fruit and fire; Jesus says a branch that does not abide is thrown out, withers and is burned.

basis: A dying Jesus entrusts his mother
note: The commentary’s testament scene gathers approaching death, entrusted care, and a transfer between people; Jesus from the cross gives his mother and the beloved disciple to one another.

basis: The entrusted person is received into a home
note: The commentary says trust and custody meet at death; the disciple takes Mary into his own home, carrying out the deathbed entrustment as practical care.

basis: doing truth brings deeds into light
note: The commentary joins truth with rightly placed works; John says the one who does truth comes to light so that the deeds done in God become visible.

basis: Truth as a means of release
note: The commentary joins truth to freeing a captive; Jesus says knowing the truth will make his hearers free, recasting liberation as an effect of truth.

basis: A wounded traveler carried on an animal
note: The commentary’s road and burden imagery turns toward care; the Samaritan binds the robbed traveler’s wounds and places him on his own animal, converting a dangerous road encounter into help.

basis: traveller lifts wounded man onto his animal
note: The commentary's hard road includes a beast, a burden and practical rescue; the Samaritan treats the injured man and carries him on his own animal to shelter.

basis: barns enlarged to store harvest
note: The commentary treats late accumulated fruit as vulnerable capital; the rich fool builds larger barns for all his grain and goods just before the death sentence in Luke 12:20.

basis: Stored harvest interrupted by death
note: The commentary’s aged gardener loses the yield before enjoying it; Jesus’ rich farmer plans many years around his abundant stores, then is told that his life ends that night.

basis: death on the night stored goods seem secure
note: The commentary's old gardener loses a lifetime's yield when it should become useful; the rich fool is called to die just after planning to store his crop, and the question asks who receives it.

basis: storing for oneself versus true wealth
note: The commentary says hoarded yield can be lost at the moment of use; Jesus concludes the rich fool's story by contrasting self-stored treasure with wealth toward God.

basis: give to poor and store imperishable treasure
note: The commentary opposes spent principal to what is safely kept through mutual help; Jesus commands almsgiving and treasure where it does not fail.

basis: One more year for a fruitless tree
note: The commentary overlaps orchard, aging time, and the risk of losing fruit; the gardener asks for one more year to tend the barren fig tree, making patience a limited extension before judgment.

basis: Faithfulness with wealth and entrusted riches
note: The commentary’s debt verse brings commerce and trust together; Jesus asks who will entrust true riches to someone unfaithful with worldly wealth.

basis: wealthy life and hungry suffering reversed after death
note: The commentary's stored plenty can end in loss beside unmet hunger; Abraham tells the rich man that Lazarus now receives comfort while he suffers, reversing their earthly shares.

basis: endurance gains life
note: The commentary sets human loss against sabr as self-restraint and preservation; Jesus says his addressees will gain their lives through endurance amid persecution.

basis: proclaim release to captives
note: The commentary makes the steep ascent an act of releasing the held person; Jesus' synagogue reading announces release to captives and freedom for the oppressed.

basis: hold word and bear fruit with endurance
note: The commentary joins holding, fruitful work and sabr as kept substance; Jesus' good soil consists of hearers who hold the word and bear fruit through endurance.

basis: sell possessions and give to poor to gain treasure
note: The commentary's hard ascent includes release from holding wealth and feeding the needy; Jesus tells the rich man to give his sale proceeds to poor people and follow him.

basis: wealth keeps a would-be follower from the path
note: The commentary's hard climb requires releasing what is held; the rich man leaves Jesus grieving because he has many possessions after being told to give them away.

basis: Profit that costs one’s life
note: The commentary describes human life as capital that can melt into loss; Jesus asks what is gained by acquiring the whole world if one forfeits oneself.

basis: profit whole world and forfeit life
note: The commentary calls the human being a trader whose principal is lost; Jesus asks what profit remains if gaining the world costs one's life.

basis: A yoke and burden made light
note: The commentary defines the ascent through a burden and a freed neck; Jesus describes his own yoke as easy and burden as light, recasting burden as sustaining discipleship.

basis: obedience defines kinship
note: The commentary shifts from ancestry that fails to a community formed by deeds; Jesus calls those who do his Father's will his brother, sister and mother.

basis: A person sells all to gain hidden treasure
note: The commentary names buying error as a ruinous bargain; Jesus’ parable reverses the valuation, as a man sells what he has to gain a treasure worth more.

basis: two or three witnesses establish the matter
note: The commentary asks which testimony is truer after a contested bequest; Jesus directs a dispute to witnesses so a matter can be established.

basis: master releases debtor and cancels loan
note: The commentary puts restraint, debt and release in one scene; the master lets a servant go and forgives an unpayable debt.

basis: forgiven debtor seizes his debtor by the throat
note: The commentary's holding image collides with a debt transaction; a newly forgiven servant physically grips another servant and demands repayment.

basis: unmerciful creditor jails debtor
note: The commentary joins debt, confinement and the choice to release; the servant instead casts his fellow servant into prison until payment.

basis: one late hour weighed against whole day of labour
note: The commentary's late hour, work and rightful payment converge; early vineyard workers complain that the last workers' single hour received equal pay.

basis: vineyard labourers paid at evening
note: The commentary treats the day as spent capital whose end reveals its yield; the vineyard owner orders wages paid when evening arrives.

basis: Feed the hungry
note: The commentary makes feeding the hungry part of the difficult ascent; in Jesus’ judgment scene, feeding the hungry is named as a deed by which people answer the king.

basis: feeding hungry and receiving stranger
note: The commentary's difficult path includes feeding during hunger; the king identifies food given to the hungry and welcome to the stranger as acts done for him.

basis: Visit the imprisoned
note: The commentary pairs release from captivity with feeding; Jesus’ judgment scene separately names visiting a person in prison, connecting practical care to final reckoning.

basis: prison visitation beside bodily care
note: The commentary holds release, hunger and communal help in one walk; the king names visiting him in prison beside clothing the naked and caring for sickness.

basis: failure to feed hungry exposed in judgment
note: The commentary places feeding on the difficult path toward final accountability; the judge condemns those who withheld food when he was hungry.

basis: ancestry from Abraham cannot be assumed as security
note: The commentary imagines lineage severed before assessment; John warns his hearers that claiming Abraham as father will not secure their standing.

basis: A general ban on swearing
note: The commentary’s witness scene uses an oath to establish a bequest; Jesus’ sermon tells disciples not to swear, giving a contrasting ethic for truthful speech.

basis: simple yes and no instead of elaborate oaths
note: The commentary's testament scene needs a formal oath to safeguard disputed truth; Jesus demands plain truthful speech beyond oath formulas, a deliberate contrast in how assurance is secured.

basis: Earthly treasure can be destroyed or stolen
note: The commentary’s accumulated fruit and capital remain vulnerable; Jesus warns that earthly stores are exposed to moth, corrosion, and thieves.

basis: wise builder sets house on rock
note: The commentary's spider house is a failed shelter; Jesus' hearer who acts on his words makes a sound house on rock, supplying the constructive counterpart to the storm's collapse.

basis: A house stands through rain and wind
note: The commentary juxtaposes ruined gardens with refuge; Jesus’ house on rock survives rain, floods, and wind because its builder acts on his words.

basis: hears words but does not do them
note: The commentary makes right works the secure building against the spider house; Jesus identifies the foolish sand builder as one who hears his words yet fails to act on them.

basis: A house collapses in the storm
note: The commentary calls the spider’s house an inadequate refuge and describes a storm ruining a garden; Jesus’ house built on sand falls when rain, flood, and wind strike.

basis: rain, floods and wind bring down a house
note: The commentary's shelter image fails under destructive weather; Jesus' house built on sand collapses when rain, floods and wind strike it.

basis: former slave received as a brother
note: The commentary's journey turns captivity and enmity into a community; Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus beyond the slave relationship as a beloved brother.

basis: Another’s debt charged to Paul
note: The commentary’s testament and debt scenes make obligation transferable; Paul tells Philemon to charge any debt or wrong by Onesimus to him.

basis: charge a brother's debt to the intercessor
note: The commentary joins release with debt and a guarantor; Paul offers to have anything Onesimus owes charged to Paul's own account.

basis: A written promise to repay
note: The commentary joins a financial obligation to trust; Paul says he writes in his own hand that he will repay, turning personal assurance into a written pledge.

basis: personal written promise to repay
note: The commentary's testament scene ties written custody, obligation and faithful surety; Paul says he writes the repayment pledge with his own hand.

basis: A message sweet in the mouth and bitter inside
note: The commentary calls patience a bitter essence kept and passed on; John eats a scroll that tastes sweet and turns bitter in his stomach, making internalized truth costly.

basis: A received message must be spoken onward
note: The commentary ends with truth and patience changing hands; after eating the scroll, John is told to prophesy again to peoples and nations, connecting inward reception to transmission.

basis: captivity and endurance of the saints
note: The commentary makes holding and captivity meet patience; Revelation speaks of captivity and immediately names the endurance and faith of the saints.

basis: Faithful community defined by endurance
note: The commentary gathers belief, right action, and patience in a community; Revelation names the saints’ endurance together with keeping God’s commands and faith in Jesus.

basis: endurance, commandments and faith together
note: The commentary closes with faith, right deeds and patience held by a people; Revelation calls for the endurance of saints who keep God's commands and faith in Jesus.

basis: deeds follow the dead after labour ends
note: The commentary sees an end of working time followed by assessment of what was preserved; Revelation promises rest from labour while the dead believers' works accompany them.

basis: Ripe grapes cast into the winepress of judgment
note: The commentary layers fruit, pressing, and the end; Revelation gathers ripe grapes and casts them into God’s great winepress, making the press a harvest image of judgment.

basis: Merchants’ wealth lost in one hour
note: The commentary compresses accumulated produce and capital into sudden loss; Revelation says Babylon’s great wealth is laid waste in one hour, as merchants watch their trade collapse.

basis: imprisonment tests faithfulness until death
note: The commentary brings detention, patience and the end of life into one movement; the Smyrna assembly is warned of prison and urged to remain faithful unto death for the crown of life.

basis: works, labour and endurance named together
note: The commentary closes with faith translated into good work and patience; the risen speaker says he knows the Ephesian assembly's works, labour and endurance.

basis: The dead judged by recorded deeds
note: The commentary joins the loss of kinship with personal weighing; Revelation depicts the dead judged from books according to what they had done.

basis: dead judged by written record of works
note: The commentary moves from broken lineage and light scales to a day confronting each person with deeds; the dead stand for judgment according to what is recorded of their works.

basis: kept word of endurance and promised protection
note: The commentary's preserved essence is reciprocal fidelity under pressure; Christ says the assembly kept his word of endurance and promises to keep it from the coming hour of trial.

basis: Feed an enemy
note: The commentary’s movement from enmity to fellowship has a concrete ethic in Paul’s instruction to feed a hungry enemy, answering hostility with care.

basis: storing wrath for judgment day
note: The commentary contrasts keeping a life-giving essence with buying fire through stubbornness; Paul says an unrepentant heart stores wrath for the coming day.

basis: Each repaid according to deeds
note: The commentary says the day confronts everyone with their work; Paul states that God repays each person according to deeds.

basis: each repaid according to deeds
note: The commentary's truth includes a day that faces everyone with their work; Paul says God renders to each person according to deeds.

basis: Patient persistence in good work
note: The commentary’s exception to loss joins belief, good deeds, and patience; Paul describes those who persist patiently in good work as seeking glory and eternal life.

basis: Affliction produces endurance
note: The commentary imagines pressure and patience meeting; Paul says suffering produces endurance, interpreting hardship as a source of steadfastness rather than only loss.

basis: vine and supporting elm represent reciprocal aid
note: The commentary's productive vine and joined community meet in Hermas's vine that bears fruit with the elm's support; the allegory applies this to rich and poor helping each other materially and in prayer.

basis: self, others and the present hour
note: The commentary moves from an isolated endangered person into mutual responsibility under dwindling time; Hillel asks what he is if only for himself and, finally, if not now, when.

basis: Short day, much work, pressing master
note: The commentary treats time as expiring capital and deeds as urgent; Tarfon says the day is short, the work abundant, and the Master of the House presses, joining time, labor, and accountability.

basis: short day, much work, pressing master
note: The commentary's asr is a late, pressing interval in which deeds must be done; Rabbi Tarfon pictures a short day, much work, workers and a pressing master in one labour account.

basis: Do not desist from unfinished work
note: The commentary’s closing community keeps transmitting good action within limited time; Tarfon says one need not finish the work but is not free to desist, adding persistence without claiming control of the outcome.

basis: Good deeds as advocates and a shield
note: The commentary says deeds distinguish those who escape loss; Avot pictures a commandment as an advocate and repentance with good deeds as a shield against punishment.

basis: This life as a vestibule before the next world
note: The commentary treats time as a limited span whose use determines what follows; Avot compares this world to a vestibule in which one prepares before entering the banquet hall.

basis: Good deeds as fruit and principal
note: The commentary makes good works the lasting yield of time; Peah says certain deeds bear fruit in this world while their principal remains for the world to come, an explicit investment image.

basis: Faithful business dealings at judgment
note: The commentary joins market trust to the day when deeds are faced; the Talmud’s first judgment question is whether one dealt faithfully in business.

basis: Remember the one who stood as guarantor
note: The commentary calls patience a guarantor; Sirach warns not to forget the kindness of one who guaranteed a neighbor’s debt and risked much on that person’s behalf.

basis: Promise and honesty in lending
note: The commentary brings debt together with trust; Sirach tells a lender to keep a promise and deal faithfully with the borrower, making reliability part of credit.

basis: Patience in adversity
note: The commentary treats patience as something retained through hardship; Sirach tells the faithful to accept what befalls them and be patient in humiliation.

basis: Faithfulness tested like gold in fire
note: The commentary’s patience has a bitter, fiery trial aspect; Sirach says the faithful are tested in the furnace of humiliation as gold is tested in fire.

basis: deliver oppressed person from oppressor
note: The commentary's way over the steep rise frees a captive; Sirach instructs the reader to deliver an oppressed person from the oppressor and not shrink from judging a case.

basis: bread for hungry and clothing for naked
note: The commentary's hard ascent includes concrete food and freedom for the vulnerable; Tobit instructs his son to give bread to hungry people and clothing to those without it.

basis: false sworn witnesses cause Naboth's death
note: The commentary's testament scene makes truth in testimony decisive; two men testify falsely against Naboth and he is killed, showing the stakes of a corrupt witness.

basis: own recollection: Arabic عصر / Hebrew עצר
note: The commentary joins pressing, withholding and rain; Solomon speaks of heaven being shut so that rain does not fall, using עצר, a possible cognate of source wording عصر whose sense here is restraint, not fruit pressing.

basis: abandoned servant fed until revived
note: The commentary's difficult road includes feeding and releasing the held or neglected person; David's men give an Egyptian bread, water and fruit after his master abandoned him.

basis: return captive brothers
note: The commentary turns confinement and enmity into brotherhood; Oded calls the captives brothers and orders their captors to send them back.

basis: captives fed, clothed and carried on donkeys
note: The commentary's ascent joins freed prisoners, food, a load animal and restored company; Judean captives are clothed, fed, anointed and carried on donkeys back to their kin.

basis: A creditor threatens to take a widow’s sons as slaves
note: The commentary brings debt and release from captivity together; the widow’s unpaid debt puts her sons at risk of enslavement, making the financial obligation a threat to family freedom.

basis: creditor threatens to enslave widow's sons
note: The commentary makes debt, captivity and threatened family loss one scene; a widow says her creditor has come to take her two sons as slaves.

basis: Oil sold to pay debt and preserve a livelihood
note: The commentary’s debt and release scenes meet in Elisha’s instruction: the widow sells the multiplied oil, pays the creditor, and lives on what remains.

basis: oil sold to pay debt and sustain family
note: The commentary joins pressed yield, rescue from debt and continuing provision; Elisha tells the widow to sell her oil, pay the creditor and live on the remainder.

basis: feed captured enemies instead of killing them
note: The commentary's path frees those held and feeds the hungry; Elisha tells the king to give captured Arameans bread and water so they may return to their master.

basis: feast ends enemy raids
note: The commentary moves from struggle to company through release and food; after the captured Arameans eat and leave, their raiding bands cease entering Israel.

basis: Summer fruit announces the end
note: The commentary layers ripe produce with life’s late hour and the end of time; Amos’s basket of summer fruit signals that Israel’s end has arrived, making harvest itself an omen of ending.

basis: poor bought for silver while grain is sold
note: The commentary's wrong bargain intersects hunger and bondage; Amos condemns merchants who sell grain while buying the needy for silver and the poor for sandals.

basis: Faithfulness chosen despite the furnace
note: The commentary calls condemned people’s readiness for fire a perverse patience; Daniel’s three youths accept the possibility of fire rather than worship another god, reversing what endurance serves.

basis: kingdom's numbered days brought to an end
note: The commentary places human loss inside spent time before the next verse's scale; Daniel first interprets the writing as Belshazzar's numbered, completed reign.

basis: Weighed and found wanting
note: The commentary links severed kinship to scales that come up light; Daniel’s wall-writing scene weighs a king and finds him wanting, making weight a verdict on conduct.

basis: weighed in scales and found wanting
note: The commentary pairs severed supports with light weight in the final balance; Daniel's verdict on Belshazzar finds him deficient when weighed.

basis: own recollection: Arabic خسر / Biblical Aramaic חסיר
note: The commentary's losing human is found light in a balance; Daniel's Aramaic verdict says the king was found lacking, with חסיר plausibly corresponding to source wording خسر; the historical cognacy needs checking.

basis: rain supports grain, wine and oil
note: The commentary's garden links rain to produce that can be pressed; Deuteronomy promises seasonal rain so grain, wine and oil can be gathered, without Joseph's explicit rescue scene.

basis: freed servant must not leave empty-handed
note: The commentary's steep path joins release with practical provision; Deuteronomy says a freed servant must not be sent away empty-handed.

basis: A freed servant sent away with produce
note: The commentary defines the ascent through freeing a captive and feeding the hungry; Deuteronomy says not to send a released servant away empty-handed but to provide from flock, threshing floor, and winepress.

basis: provision from flock, threshing floor and winepress
note: The commentary links freeing a captive with feeding and pressed yield; Deuteronomy orders gifts from animals, grain and winepress to the departing servant.

basis: Release of debts
note: The commentary develops debt as one face of truth; Deuteronomy commands release of loans at the appointed remission, connecting obligation to mercy within the community.

basis: Two or three witnesses establish a matter
note: The commentary’s deathbed bequest depends on witnesses; Deuteronomy likewise rejects a single witness and requires two or three for a charge.

basis: two witnesses establish a matter
note: The commentary's deathbed testament weighs witnesses and the truer claim; Deuteronomy requires two or three witnesses for a matter to stand.

basis: creditor must not enter debtor's house for pledge
note: The commentary joins marketplace debt with custody of an entrusted thing; Deuteronomy restrains the lender's power over a pledged object.

basis: return pledged cloak before sunset
note: The commentary's debt meets the passing day and the duty to return what was held; the lender must give back the poor debtor's cloak by sunset so he can sleep in it.

basis: widow's garment must not be pledged
note: The commentary joins truthful judgment to the restraint of collateral; Deuteronomy forbids perverting the vulnerable person's justice and taking a widow's garment as a pledge.

basis: forgotten harvest left for vulnerable people
note: The commentary's stored yield meets an obligation to feed on the hard path; Deuteronomy leaves a forgotten sheaf to stranger, orphan and widow rather than reclaiming it.

basis: Every deed brought into judgment
note: The commentary says the day makes each person face their work; Ecclesiastes says every deed, including what is hidden, comes into judgment.

basis: Light and rain clouds dim before old age
note: The commentary layers life’s late afternoon with rain and its destructive turn; Ecclesiastes pictures sun, moon, and stars darkening and clouds returning after rain in its approach to death.

basis: own recollection: Arabic عمل / Hebrew עמל
note: The commentary's right work should remain while spent life can be lost; Ecclesiastes hates toil that must be left to a successor, using עמל, a possible consonantal cognate of source wording عمل with a darker sense.

basis: A companion lifts the fallen
note: The commentary’s steep path and transition into togetherness meet Ecclesiastes’ image of one companion raising another who falls on the road of life.

basis: companion lifts the fallen
note: The commentary changes a solitary difficult ascent into mutual support; Ecclesiastes says one companion raises the other after a fall.

basis: A cord holds companions together
note: The commentary reads holding together as rescue from danger; Ecclesiastes says a three-strand cord is not quickly broken, giving the communal bond a material image.

basis: threefold cord withstands rupture
note: The commentary's rope joins grasping, company and rescue from an edge; Ecclesiastes' cord of three strands makes solidarity itself resistant to breaking.

basis: Wealth perishes in a bad venture
note: The commentary’s garden loses its accumulated yield at the moment of expectation; Ecclesiastes describes wealth kept to its owner’s hurt and lost through a disastrous venture.

basis: A pledged garment returned before sunset
note: The commentary joins debt, holding, and release within passing time; Exodus requires a creditor to return a poor borrower’s garment by sunset, so the pledge cannot become lasting captivity.

basis: pledged garment returned by sunset
note: The commentary's debt scene joins held collateral to a spent day; Exodus also requires returning a poor person's pledged cloak before the sun goes down.

basis: Lift an enemy’s overloaded donkey
note: The commentary moves from struggle toward companionship and mentions a beast of burden; Torah commands helping even an enemy’s donkey rise under its load, making cooperation concrete.

basis: Righteousness cannot be transferred to a child
note: The commentary places severed kinship beside individual weighing; Ezekiel says even Noah, Daniel, and Job could save only themselves, not sons or daughters, so family ties do not transfer standing.

basis: child does not carry parent's guilt
note: The commentary sets severed genealogical ties beside individual weighing; Ezekiel denies transfer of a father's guilt to a son, making personal conduct decisive.

basis: fruitful vine uprooted and dried by east wind
note: The commentary's planted fruit is destroyed after growth by a violent wind; Ezekiel's lament uproots a fruitful vine and has the east wind dry its fruit.

basis: bricks made for collective city project
note: The commentary's believers fit together like sound bricks for helpful works; Babel's people likewise make bricks together, but their shared building becomes a project of self-exaltation and dispersal.

basis: own recollection: Arabic آمنوا / Hebrew אמן
note: The commentary says believers enter safety; Genesis says Abram believed the Lord and that trust was reckoned to him as righteousness, giving a specific faith-and-right-standing use of the corresponding root.

basis: Esau sells his birthright
note: The commentary's bad purchase exchanges lasting value for ruinous immediate gain; Esau swears away his birthright for the meal offered by Jacob.

basis: vine ripens before pressing dream
note: The commentary links growing fruit with squeezing in Joseph's prison; the cupbearer's dream first presents a budding vine whose clusters ripen before the pressing action in Genesis 40:11.

basis: Joseph in prison; grapes pressed into Pharaoh’s cup
note: The commentary joins Joseph’s confinement to pressing; in Joseph’s prison story the cupbearer dreams of squeezing grapes into Pharaoh’s cup, while the dream belongs to the cupbearer.

basis: Joseph's imprisoned cupbearer squeezes grapes
note: The commentary puts squeezing beside detention in Joseph's prison; the cupbearer presses grapes into Pharaoh's cup inside his prison dream, giving that pairing a concrete narrative scene.

basis: cupbearer released after three days
note: The commentary moves from prison's restraint to relief; Joseph tells the imprisoned cupbearer he will be restored to service, a specific release following the pressing dream.

basis: Joseph forgotten in confinement
note: The commentary pairs Joseph’s prison with patience; after the cupbearer is restored, he forgets Joseph, adding the concrete delay of being left confined and unremembered.

basis: Two years pass before Joseph is recalled
note: The commentary makes detention and patience meet; Genesis marks two full years before Pharaoh’s dream brings the imprisoned Joseph back into view, specifying the length of the wait.

basis: seven years of abundance
note: The commentary's year of provision follows Joseph's prediction; Joseph announces years of plenty before scarcity, making productive time something to preserve.

basis: seven years of famine
note: The commentary pairs the fruitful year with threatened loss; Joseph says famine will consume the prior abundance, turning accumulated yield into a question of survival.

basis: food stored against famine
note: The commentary's rain, pressing and rescue culminate in usable provision; Joseph proposes keeping grain so the land will not perish in famine.

basis: Joseph stores the abundant harvest
note: The commentary’s Yusuf year makes relief follow scarcity; Genesis has Joseph gather the abundant years’ produce into storehouses so the later famine can be survived.

basis: Joseph holds brothers in custody during famine
note: The commentary makes Joseph's food rescue meet detention; Joseph confines his brothers for three days while testing those who seek grain.

basis: one brother detained while others carry food home
note: The commentary joins alıkonma to sustenance; Joseph holds one brother as security and sends the others with grain for their hungry households.

basis: Joseph promises food during famine
note: The commentary makes Joseph's good year a deliverance for people; Joseph promises to sustain his family through the remaining famine years.

basis: Joseph sent ahead to preserve survivors
note: The commentary's good year turns pressing and food into communal rescue; Joseph interprets his arrival in Egypt as a means of preserving a remnant through famine.

basis: A dying patriarch asks for an oath about burial
note: The commentary’s testament scene joins approaching death, trust, and obligation; Jacob, near death, asks Joseph to swear that he will not bury him in Egypt.

basis: dying Jacob binds Joseph by oath
note: The commentary's testament scene unites death, custody and sworn duty; dying Jacob requires Joseph's pledged hand and loyal burial promise.

basis: The deathbed request is secured by an oath
note: The commentary places oath and bequest together at death; Joseph swears to Jacob’s burial request, turning a dying person’s instruction into an entrusted duty.

basis: A final oath entrusted to the next generation
note: The commentary joins death, custody, and what passes between people; Joseph makes Israel’s descendants swear to carry his bones when God visits them.

basis: Joseph's burial oath entrusted to descendants
note: The commentary's testament binds witnesses and future custodians across death; Joseph makes Israelites swear to carry his bones when God brings them out.

basis: own recollection: Arabic آمنوا / Hebrew אמן
note: The commentary's believers endure and do right; Habakkuk says the righteous person will live by faithfulness, applying the corresponding root to sustained fidelity under crisis.

basis: Wages vanish into a bag with holes
note: The commentary says human capital melts away; Haggai pictures earned wages disappearing into a bag with holes, tying loss to futile labor.

basis: wages put into a bag with holes
note: The commentary pictures a person's principal steadily eroding; Haggai names meagre harvest and wages that disappear as though stored in a perforated purse.

basis: sow wind and reap whirlwind
note: The commentary's fruitful garden is erased by a whirlwind at the point of yield; Hosea makes a whirlwind the harvest of a disastrous sowing, linking crop and loss in one image.

basis: own recollection: Arabic حق / Hebrew חקק
note: The commentary expects an unswerving claim of right; Isaiah condemns rulers who decree unjust decrees using חקק, a possible cognate of source wording حق that also shows a contrary use of legal authority.

basis: Shelter from storm and heat
note: The commentary layers refuge with rain and tempest; Isaiah pictures a just ruler as shelter from wind and storm, a safe counterpart to the fragile garden or web.

basis: breath withers flower and grass
note: The commentary's rain-grown fruit is exposed to destructive weather and passing life; Isaiah says the divine breath dries grass and fades flowers as an image of human frailty.

basis: Human growth fades while the word endures
note: The commentary moves from mortal time to truth that is transmitted and kept; Isaiah contrasts fading grass and flowers with the enduring word of God.

basis: word remains after vegetation fades
note: The commentary ends with a preserved and transmitted essence after loss; Isaiah says God's word stands forever when grass and flowers fail.

basis: Vineyard, grapes, and winepress
note: The commentary’s garden contains grapes and fruit meant for pressing; Isaiah’s cultivated vineyard has a winepress prepared for its expected grapes, though its yield proves different.

basis: A vineyard ruined when rain is withheld
note: The commentary’s garden is destroyed by a sudden storm after fruitfulness; Isaiah instead makes a failed vineyard waste and withholds rain, a distinct judgment pattern.

basis: vineyard deprived of rain after judgment
note: The commentary's rain-grown garden can be lost in a single turn; Isaiah's judged vineyard is denied rain after its owner abandons its care, a reversed weather detail.

basis: spend wages on what fails to nourish
note: The commentary's human loses principal through a false purchase; Isaiah asks why people spend money on what is not bread and labour on what does not satisfy.

basis: feed hungry and light rises in darkness
note: The commentary links feeding, mutual care and the transition of night into day; Isaiah says satisfying the hungry makes darkness like noonday.

basis: well-watered garden whose waters do not fail
note: The commentary's rain-grown garden faces devastating loss; Isaiah promises the one who feeds the afflicted an unfailing watered garden, the positive outcome of the same food scene.

basis: Release the bound and break the yoke
note: The commentary defines the steep ascent through freeing a captive; Isaiah’s fast is to loose wicked bonds, undo the yoke, and let the oppressed go free.

basis: loose bonds and free oppressed people
note: The commentary explains the hard ascent by undoing a captive's neck; Isaiah defines the chosen fast by undoing unjust bonds and sending the oppressed free.

basis: Give bread to the hungry
note: The commentary names feeding on a day of hunger as part of the ascent; Isaiah places sharing bread with the hungry in the same account of true fasting.

basis: share bread with hungry and shelter poor
note: The commentary places feeding on a day of hunger after release; Isaiah immediately pairs liberation with sharing bread with hungry people and bringing the homeless in.

basis: wicked people weave spider webs
note: The commentary contrasts useful weaving with the spider's false house; Isaiah names spider webs among the works produced by violent, deceitful people.

basis: Spider webs cannot clothe
note: The commentary links the spider’s house to textile and failed protection; Isaiah says webs cannot serve as garments, making the woven product useless as covering.

basis: spider webs cannot become clothing
note: The commentary opposes the spider's weaving to secure covering; Isaiah says woven webs cannot cover their makers, while their deeds are violent.

basis: own recollection: Arabic آمنوا / Hebrew אמן
note: The commentary joins belief with a secure standing amid loss; Isaiah warns that unless his hearers trust, they will not be established, a Hebrew play on two forms of אמן.

basis: tree by water continues fruit in drought
note: The commentary's lifetime garden fails under destructive weather; Jeremiah's trusting person is a rooted tree whose leaves stay green and fruit continues even in drought.

basis: The word as fire and a rock-breaking hammer
note: The commentary gives truth the image of a straight blow; Jeremiah compares God’s word to fire and a hammer that breaks rock, making truthful speech forceful rather than merely abstract.

basis: Signed deed, witnesses, and weighed silver
note: The commentary says the debt scene joins market and trust; Jeremiah records a land purchase with a signed deed, witnesses, and silver weighed out, a close transactional analogue.

basis: Sealed deeds kept in an earthen vessel
note: The commentary joins financial trust to preserved contents; Jeremiah orders sealed and open copies of the deed stored in a jar so they last, showing custody protecting a transaction.

basis: freed servants forcibly taken back
note: The commentary's steep path releases a captive into fellowship; Jeremiah condemns people who reverse a prior manumission and bring their servants back into bondage.

basis: Ropes pull Jeremiah out of a pit
note: The commentary says a community is pulled back from an edge; Jeremiah is physically drawn from a cistern by ropes, a concrete rescue image with a different meaning from the shared covenant rope.

basis: men haul Jeremiah from a pit with ropes
note: The commentary's road joins a burden, holding and release; Ebed-melech's men pull Jeremiah up with ropes from confinement in a cistern, a literal collective rescue.

basis: Fire consumes accumulated flocks and servants
note: The commentary’s ruined garden includes a destructive fiery storm; in Job’s sequence of calamities, fire from heaven consumes sheep and servants, one part of the sudden loss of his holdings.

basis: A violent wind destroys a house amid accumulated loss
note: The commentary makes a whirlwind erase what was gathered; Job’s children die when a great wind collapses the house during their feast, after earlier losses of property.

basis: just balance for moral assessment
note: The commentary's loss is pictured as being light on a scale; Job invites God to weigh him on an honest balance to know his integrity.

basis: Trust as a spider’s web
note: The commentary makes the spider house a refuge that fails; Job says the confidence of the godless is like a spider’s web, matching the fragile shelter image.

basis: trust like a spider's web
note: The commentary sets the spider house against real refuge; Bildad describes the godless person's confidence as a spider's web, making apparently woven support precarious.

basis: house fails when leaned upon
note: The commentary's spider house is a false shelter; Bildad says the godless person leans on his house but it does not stand, carrying the web image into failed reliance.

basis: threshing floors full and vats overflow
note: The commentary's good side of the year is stored produce and pressing; Joel imagines restored abundance filling floors with grain and vats with wine and oil.

basis: years consumed by locusts restored
note: The commentary pictures a lifetime's accumulated crop erased; Joel answers lost productive years with a promise to restore what successive locust swarms consumed.

basis: scarlet cord marks a house for rescue
note: The commentary's rope combines attachment with group safety at a deadly edge; Rahab is told to bind a scarlet cord in the window and gather her family in the house.

basis: family must remain inside the cord-marked house
note: The commentary moves from individual grasp to shared safety; Rahab's household is safe within the marked house but not if members go outside.

basis: Rahab's family brought out together
note: The commentary links a cord to collective escape from the edge; Joshua's scouts bring Rahab and her whole family out when the city falls, completing the cord-marked rescue of Joshua 2:18.

basis: own recollection: Arabic عصر / Hebrew עצר
note: The commentary pairs squeezing with detention; Manoah asks the visitor to remain, using Hebrew עצר for holding someone back, a possible consonantal cognate of source wording عصر whose relationship needs verification.

basis: vineyard gleanings left to poor and stranger
note: The commentary's grapes and hunger belong to one ethical landscape; Leviticus leaves the ungleaned vineyard fruit for poor people and foreigners.

basis: just weights required in trade
note: The commentary's market meets truthful, unswerving measure and the final scale; Leviticus orders honest balances, weights and measures.

basis: Witness called under oath
note: The commentary gathers oath, testimony, and truth at the moment of a bequest; Leviticus treats hearing a public oath and withholding testimony as a legal offense.

basis: false commercial scales cannot be acquitted
note: The commentary joins the market, truthful measurement and light weight in judgment; Micah asks whether wicked scales and deceitful weights could be treated as innocent.

basis: restore vineyards and pledged goods
note: The commentary links debt, fruit-bearing land and release from a creditor's hold; Nehemiah demands the immediate return of fields, vineyards and financial claims.

basis: children enslaved through debt and lost fields
note: The commentary's bad market strips a household of both future and freedom; Nehemiah's complainants say their children are forced into slavery while their fields and vineyards belong to others.

basis: Honest weights in trade
note: The commentary brings market trust and truthful judgment together; Proverbs condemns false scales and approves accurate weights in commerce.

basis: dishonest balance versus just weight
note: The commentary's market bargain meets the scale that tests moral worth; Proverbs opposes fraudulent scales to an accurate weight pleasing to God.

basis: giving increases, withholding causes want
note: The commentary's bad exchange loses capital whereas shared goods preserve a community; Proverbs reverses ordinary accounting by contrasting generous increase with possessive want.

basis: own recollection: Arabic خسر / Hebrew חסר
note: The commentary's loss is a dwindling principal; this proverb says possessive withholding leads to want, using Hebrew מחסור from חסר, a plausible but unverified cognate of the source's خسر.

basis: one who waters others is watered
note: The commentary's rain and preserved yield become reciprocal support; Proverbs makes refreshment flow back to the person who refreshes others.

basis: Riches fail on the day of wrath
note: The commentary contrasts loss with deeds that carry a person through judgment; Proverbs says riches cannot deliver on the day of wrath but righteousness delivers from death.

basis: wealth useless on day of wrath
note: The commentary's spent principal meets the day that exposes what remains; Proverbs says riches cannot help on the day of wrath, whereas righteousness delivers.

basis: A seemingly right road ends in death
note: The commentary describes the human as straying within time; Proverbs warns that a way can seem right yet end in death, specifying the danger of misjudgment.

basis: true witness saves lives
note: The commentary's testament scene weighs truthful against corrupt testimony; Proverbs says a truthful witness delivers lives while a deceitful witness speaks lies.

basis: Patience as rule over oneself
note: The commentary reads sabr as self-restraint; Proverbs says ruling one’s spirit is greater than taking a city, making inner restraint the achievement.

basis: feeding poor treated as a loan repaid by God
note: The commentary puts debt and support of the needy together; Proverbs casts kindness to a poor person as lending to the Lord, who repays.

basis: debtor's bed taken for lack of payment
note: The commentary imagines capital eroding and security forfeited in a bad transaction; Proverbs asks why a guarantor would risk having even his bed seized.

basis: buy truth and do not sell it
note: The commentary places truth beside the bad bargain where lasting value is spent; Proverbs makes truth something to acquire and keep rather than trade away.

basis: Wealth grows wings and flies away
note: The commentary makes stored capital vulnerable to sudden disappearance; Proverbs pictures riches sprouting wings and flying off, turning possession into impermanence.

basis: rescue people being taken to death
note: The commentary's hard ascent includes releasing someone held at a lethal edge; Proverbs commands intervention for people being led to death.

basis: God weighs hearts and repays rescue omitted
note: The commentary sets the rescue duty beside weighing and final recompense; the following proverb rejects the excuse of ignorance because the keeper of souls weighs hearts and repays deeds.

basis: give bread to a hungry enemy
note: The commentary moves from contest to shared sustenance; Proverbs specifically orders feeding and watering an enemy in need.

basis: A friend’s wounds can be faithful
note: The commentary lets truth be a straight, painful blow; Proverbs says a friend’s wounds may be trusted, presenting frank correction as a form of loyalty.

basis: faithful friend's wounds
note: The commentary imagines true counsel as an unpleasant medicine retained for good; Proverbs values the wounds of a faithful friend over an enemy's plentiful kisses.

basis: Truth bound at the neck and written on the heart
note: The commentary joins truth to holding and binding; Proverbs tells the reader to bind faithfulness and truth around the neck and write them on the heart, combining tethering with inward preservation.

basis: A person becomes surety for a neighbor
note: The commentary gives patience the secondary image of a guarantor and joins trust to debt; Proverbs depicts someone pledging security for a neighbor, making the guarantee a concrete accepted burden.

basis: free yourself after becoming surety
note: The commentary gives sabr a guarantor sense while its path frees the constrained; Proverbs depicts a debt guarantor caught in another's hand and urgently seeking release.

basis: own recollection: Arabic حق / Hebrew חקק
note: The commentary's haqq includes right judgment; Wisdom says rulers decree justice using חקק, consonantally close to source wording حق, though the historical relation between right and engraved decree is uncertain.

basis: Meditating on instruction day and night
note: The commentary says communal counsel joins like night and day; the psalmist meditates on Torah day and night, making ethical instruction a sustained practice across time.

basis: A righteous tree bears fruit in season and does not wither
note: The commentary’s fruitful garden is destroyed at the moment of expected yield; Psalm 1 pictures the righteous as a watered tree whose seasonal fruit remains, a counter-image of stability.

basis: fruitful tree by streams that does not wither
note: The commentary's lost garden contrasts with faith and fruitful works; the righteous person is a planted tree yielding fruit in season whose leaf does not wither.

basis: own recollection: Arabic الصالحات / Hebrew צלח
note: The commentary says good deeds fit and yield value; the psalm says the tree-like righteous person prospers in what he does, a possible sound and semantic cognate between source wording صلح and Hebrew צלח.

basis: Joseph fettered
note: The commentary pairs Joseph’s imprisonment with patience; the psalm retelling puts his feet in fetters and his neck in iron, making confinement part of the Joseph story.

basis: Joseph tested while awaiting the promise
note: The commentary makes patience meet detention; the next line of the psalm says the Lord’s word tested Joseph until its fulfillment, giving his confinement a waiting-for-release dimension.

basis: giving poor yields enduring righteousness
note: The commentary makes a shared gift survive the waste of time; the psalm says one who distributes to the poor has righteousness enduring forever.

basis: The word stored in the heart
note: The commentary ends with truth received and preserved; the psalmist stores God’s word in the heart as a safeguard against sin, making inward keeping an ethical act.

basis: Borrowing without repayment
note: The commentary links debt to trust; the psalm contrasts a wicked borrower who does not repay with a righteous person who gives generously.

basis: Brief lifespan and toil
note: The commentary makes a lifetime’s yield vulnerable at its late hour; the psalm counts human years as short and full of toil, then quickly gone.

basis: Numbering days to gain wisdom
note: The commentary treats time as expiring capital; the psalm asks to be taught to number one’s days so the heart may gain wisdom, turning limited time into a prompt for action.

basis: Life flourishes, then withers at evening
note: The commentary reads asr as the evening of a life; the psalm compares human flourishing to grass that sprouts in the morning and withers by evening.

basis: God as refuge and fortress
note: The commentary contrasts a spider’s false shelter with real security; the psalm names God as refuge and fortress, supplying a contrasting image of protection.

basis: Fruit still borne in old age
note: The commentary’s old owner loses his garden as age advances; the psalm instead pictures the righteous still bearing fruit in old age, a concrete counter-image of fruitful late life.

basis: Speak truth to one another
note: The commentary’s mutual counsel is centered on truth; Zechariah commands neighbors to speak truth and render judgments that make for peace.

basis: speak truth to neighbour and judge truly
note: The commentary treats haqq as a thing passed mutually and as a sound verdict; Zechariah commands true speech to neighbours and truthful judgment at the gates.

basis: false oath prohibited among neighbours
note: The commentary's bequest joins oath and truth with reciprocal duty; Zechariah forbids loving false oaths as part of the same neighbourly justice expressed in Zechariah 8:16.
